dialogue.content: tuned everything and then went to bed.
played something I half-know a few times through.
showed someone the thing I'm proud of. they nodded.
did it while something was on in the background.
I assumed a piece stops teaching you once you know it. what happens instead is that with nothing left to work out, I start hearing what I'm actually doing rather than what I'm trying to do.
I did say the opposite, for years.
put a new string on and broke it immediately.
spent longer choosing what to work on than working.
wrote the date on a thing so I'd remember when.
learned a new piece properly over a month.
restrung it and immediately put it down again.
watched a tutorial all the way through without trying any of it.
reorganised the shelf by colour. took an hour.
bought a thing I already own a version of.
cleaned everything instead of using any of it.
the two habits I've ever actually fixed, I caught while playing something I'd played hundreds of times. new material hides everything behind the effort of learning it.
you can't hear yourself over the work.
found a half-finished thing at the back of a drawer.
wrote down an idea and closed the notebook.
spent the evening reading about it rather than doing it.
fixed the wobbly leg on the table finally.
